elements.label: Figure 7.9
elements.description:
Grouped vertical bar chart of percentage point change in poverty from fiscal policy, by country, grouped by World Bank income level. Y-axis: 'Percentage Point Change', from -12 to 8 in steps of 2. Legend: teal = 'Market to Disposable', orange = 'Market to Consumable'. Values are not printed; approximate readings (teal / orange) are:

High income: Poland ~-5.8 / ~-4.1; Panama ~-2.5 / ~-2.7; Chile ~-3.0 / ~-1.8; Uruguay ~-4.2 / ~-0.8.

Upper middle income: Iran, Islamic Rep. ~-11.6 / ~-10.5; Ecuador ~-3.1 / ~-3.8; Mexico ~-2.3 / ~-2.5; Jordan ~-1.0 / ~-2.1; Paraguay ~-1.6 / ~-1.6; Russian Federation ~-1.8 / ~-1.1; Mexico ~-1.7 / ~-0.9; Mexico ~-1.5 / ~-0.8; Belarus ~-0.4 / ~-0.3; Russian Federation ~-1.0 / ~-0.3; Indonesia ~0.3 / ~-0.2; South Africa ~-4.5 / ~-0.2; Colombia ~-0.8 / ~-0.1; Peru ~-0.8 / ~0.1; Argentina ~-4.9 / ~0.2; Costa Rica ~-1.5 / ~0.3; Peru ~-0.3 / ~0.6; Venezuela, RB ~-0.1 / ~0.7; Dominican Republic ~-1.0 / ~0.9; Colombia ~0.3 / ~1.4; Guatemala ~-0.2 / ~2.4; Brazil ~-1.9 / ~3.4; Albania ~-1.3 / ~6.5; Armenia ~0.1 / ~6.7.

Lower middle income: Tunisia ~-0.4 / ~-1.3; El Salvador ~-1.8 / ~-0.3; Honduras ~-0.8 / ~-0.1; Vietnam ~-0.4 / ~0.5; Bolivia ~-2.0 / ~0.5; Nicaragua ~-0.2 / ~1.1; Ghana ~0.3 / ~2.1; Sri Lanka ~-2.3 / ~2.8; Tanzania ~0.9 / ~6.2.

Lower income: Uganda ~-0.9 / ~-0.1; Ethiopia ~-0.9 / ~1.3; Burkina Faso ~-0.9 / ~5.6.

Pattern: most high-income and upper middle-income countries show negative teal bars (poverty reduction) and orange bars near zero or negative, while several lower middle-income and lower-income countries show orange bars well above zero (poverty increase), with Albania, Armenia, Tanzania and Burkina Faso among the highest orange values.
